And the Prosecution requests formally that we receive a further report from the witness if this plan is to be embarked upon by the Defence which covers this fresh material. Mr. President, finally, in relation to the report of Dr. Vilicic. In that report at page 24, the author, that is, the expert, refers to a figure, that is, a diagram or map in the report, which he describes as figure 31A. That appears in the report and is described as being drawn from "the official headquarters staff topographic map of the Serb forces." Mr. President, if that map exists and it's in the possession of the Defence, it's my submission that that should have been disclosed, if it hasn't been disclosed, to the Prosecution because it's clearly caught by the terms of reciprocal disclosure. So I'd be grateful if the Defence could identify more particularly that map, if it says that it's disclosed to the Prosecution. And if not, it should be immediately disclosed to the Prosecution on two quite separate bases. Firstly, in terms of reciprocal disclosure; but secondly, as a document which Professor Vilicic has relied on for a part of his report. The map which appears in the report appears to be comprised for the purposes of the report drawing on the information in the other map. Thank you, Mr. President.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: May I ask the Defence first to respond on the last part, whether the map the expert relies upon could be provided to the Prosecution.

utterances.speaker: MS. PILIPOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honour, bearing in mind the submission of my learned colleague, I have to say that I am a little surprised why this is done in such a way, when there was not a single moment when the Prosecution addressed themselves to the Defence. I have to examine in detail everything that my learned colleague is requesting, and I can give a response to this submission early tomorrow morning in respect of everything that my learned colleague has expressed as being a problem. I have to say that all the notes that the Defence disclosed to the Defence [as interpreted] in accordance with a decision of the Trial Chamber - and I think that the Defence in its submission -- in its motion, that it's addressed to the Trial Chamber, also explains this position. I have also disclosed the notes in accordance with your decision, but at this moment I have no idea what the problem is when the notes are concerned.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MS. PILIPOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I think I'm going to have to carefully examine all the arguments submitted by my learned colleague.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: [Previous interpretation continues] ... We'll hear from you, Ms. Pilipovic. May I give you as some guidance that the Chamber has not allowed the Prosecution to use expert reports in order to introduce new witness statements where the Defence has had no opportunity to cross-examine these witnesses. So as far as the sources are concerned, it is a very sensitive issue to what extent new facts can be introduced, and especially if they come from sources that would be sources that could have been called or that have given witness statements but where there was no possibility to cross-examine the witnesses giving these statements.

utterances.speaker: MS. PILIPOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honour, I still don't know what new facts are these, considering that Mr. Radovan Radinovic in his expert report quoted the sources that he relied upon. So I really don't know what new material, what new facts these are.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Neither do I. But I hear that the Prosecution is complaining about the introduction of new documents without witnesses to explain what these documents are, where they come from, what their content is. But I would like just to remind you that there are limits to what extent experts can introduce facts that cannot be verified, whether these are witness statements or whether these are documents. But let's not try to debate at full all the issues before we have had a better opportunity to look at whatever has been submitted and filed today. But I just gave you this guidance in order to be better able to prepare for your submissions tomorrow.

utterances.speaker: MS. PILIPOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes. Yes, Your Honour. I thank you. But in any case, I expect the submission of my learned colleagues, as Mr. Ierace has indicated.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. Then is the Prosecution ready to continue its cross-examination of Witness DP2?

utterances.speaker: MS. MAHINDARATNE
utterances.text: Yes, Mr. President.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. Then could the curtains be -- Oh, yes. Mr. Piletta-Zanin, would you mind if the curtains are already pulled down, or would it take more time? And the public gallery is not that full, as I --

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: [Interpretation] No importance, whatsoever. Perhaps it will be a good idea to ask about the tape or to find out about the tape.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. I'll ask the registrar to inform us.

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: [Interpretation] And secondly, Mr. President --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Since another registrar was serving, we need more time to retrieve that tape. So, therefore, no final decision can be taken on the tape at this very moment. Your next matter was, Mr. Piletta-Zanin ...?

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Very well. Very well. Secondly, contrary to what we have been told, Mr. President -- and so far we have not received a written decision in relation to the disqualification procedure.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: It's not my decision. I know that the President of this Chamber has taken a decision and was about to issue it in writing as well. I don't know whether it has been done today what I expected as a matter of fact. But -- but I as a Presiding Judge of this Chamber am informed about what the decision was and acted accordingly, and I'll find out or ask one of my fellow Judges to find out whether the decision has been filed. I'm certain that the decision will be put in your mailbox as soon as it has been filed. Any other issue, Mr. Piletta-Zanin? Then could the curtains be pulled down.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Ms. Mahindaratne, please proceed.

utterances.speaker: MS. MAHINDARATNE
utterances.text: Witness, I am referring to the school you spoke of. And if I may draw your attention to your testimony, page 17162. You said: "I know that primary schools, secondary schools, kindergartens and facilities were used as military facilities. About Caco's headquarters 200 metres from there, and his headquarters was just five metres above the former military command of General Kukanjac. And during the war that was the Egyptian SFOR forces. So his command was some 10 metres above -- I don't know if it was a school. I don't know what the name was. But it was a primary school and there were kitchens there and also soldiers rooms. Now, would you please indicate on the map with a blue marker where this school was. And please use a blue marker.

utterances.speaker: MS. MAHINDARATNE
utterances.text: Could the map be adjusted so that it could be seen on the ELMO.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DP2 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Caco's main staff has been marked with the number "4" and this marks the positions where the school should have been, where Caco's troops were billeted.

utterances.speaker: MS. MAHINDARATNE
utterances.text: And can you indicate -- your testimony was that -- I will use your own words "and behind that school, I went to dig the trenches." Where behind that school did you dig the trenches? Could you indicate with the blue pen where you dug trenches behind the school.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DP2 [Resumed]
utterances.text: I never said that I dug trenches behind the school. I dug trenches in Poljine, Trebevic, and that was at the beginning. I think that I marked the places then, but it's not possible to dig trenches behind the school because that is an urban area. I can't have said that.

utterances.speaker: MS. MAHINDARATNE
utterances.text: Sir, I can assure you you said that you dug trenches. In fact, let me quote your testimony back to you. You said, "And behind that school, I went to dig the trenches. So every morning we would have breakfast there and I know that because I was there every morning." That was your testimony.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. Mr. Piletta-Zanin.

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you, Mr. President. It's not that I want to interrupt anything, but I want to know -- I don't know whether the witness mentioned a number below the first circle, Bistrik. I think that should be clarified for the sake of the transcript.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: [Previous interpretation continues] ... Indicated the school is marked by the witness with a "9." Ms. Mahindaratne, if you would have told this, then we would have prevented unnecessary interruption that -- I have to say that could have been shorter as well. Please proceed.

utterances.speaker: MS. MAHINDARATNE
utterances.text: Sir, not only on the previous day did you mention that you dug trenches behind the school. Even today you mentioned that. And I refer to page 32, line 19. I will quote your testimony. "We left that school to go and dig trenches." That was your testimony.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DP2 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. MAHINDARATNE
utterances.text: You go on to say, "We also left the primary school to go and dig." So your testimony was that you dug trenches behind the school. Could you please -- is it your position that you did not dig trenches behind the school? Are you withdrawing that --

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DP2 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, even when you read out my testimony, that -- it doesn't mean that I was digging trenches behind the school. I couldn't have done so because it was an urban area. There were buildings there. I dug trenches in Poljine, near the Serbian positions, and that's high up.

utterances.speaker: MS. MAHINDARATNE
utterances.text: Witness, will you please examine the map. You have indicated four positions where you dug trenches at. In what manner did you dig these trenches? And let me qualify that question. Was it done sporadically as in did you dig trenches at one place and then move to another place and then return to that earlier place, or did you finish digging trenches at one location and then move on to the next location? Is that how it was done?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DP2 [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, never at the same location. Usually the locations were different. It depended on the group whose turn it was. Sometimes people would be taken to one location, sometimes to another.

utterances.speaker: MS. MAHINDARATNE
utterances.text: During which period did you dig trenches below the transit road of the Jewish cemetery?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DP2 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, as I said, it depended on the location that I was taken to, and this depended on the need. Sometimes I was at Jezersko [phoen], sometimes on Borije. There were four locations. Sometimes I'd go to the same location, you know, from mid-1992 up until 1994 I dug at all these locations.

utterances.speaker: MS. MAHINDARATNE
utterances.text: Very well. At what time did you start digging? I'm asking on a day that you'd be required to dig trenches, generally what time did you start digging?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DP2 [Resumed]
utterances.text: We would meet at about half past 7.00. Then it took us an hour to get to the location. We'd stay there for about five hours. In the winter we would be there for less than five hours and sometimes for over five hours in the summer.

utterances.speaker: MS. MAHINDARATNE
utterances.text: So generally at what time did you return after digging trenches?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DP2 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, about half past 3.00 in winter and about 5.00 in summer. We'd dig until about 5.00 in the afternoon.

utterances.speaker: MS. MAHINDARATNE
utterances.text: You testified that you saw weapons at the trenches. And I'm referring to testimony at page 17147. And you also mentioned that you saw two machine-guns -- I beg your pardon. I withdraw that. You saw machine-guns at two locations. What were these locations?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DP2 [Resumed]
utterances.text: I saw this at the Borije and at the Jewish cemetery.

utterances.speaker: MS. MAHINDARATNE
utterances.text: Moving on to another area, witness, how many times have you observed Sarajevo being shelled from Serb territory? Could you give an approximate number.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DP2 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, this is what I can say. Sarajevo was shelled as often as the Muslim forces wanted Sarajevo to be shelled. I've explained this.

utterances.speaker: MS. MAHINDARATNE
utterances.text: Witness, may I interrupt. I just asked you for the number, not the circumstances under which Sarajevo was shelled. I said about how many times you personally have observed, you personally have seen Sarajevo being shelled from Serb territory?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DP2 [Resumed]
utterances.text: First of all, I didn't see it on any occasion. I said that I was in the shelter. But as I said, it was shelled as often as the Muslim forces carried out attacks from Sarajevo and as often as the Serbian side was provoked to fire after the mobile mortars.

utterances.speaker: MS. MAHINDARATNE
utterances.text: So let me -- let me get this clear. Your testimony is that you personally did not see the shelling from Serb territory. My question to you is about what you saw. I'm not asking about the circumstances. And if I am -- if I may clarify. What you're saying is you personally did not see Sarajevo being shelled from Serb territory. Is that correct? Please answer yes or no.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DP2 [Resumed]
utterances.text: I saw the consequences of the shelling, but I didn't see the shelling itself.

utterances.speaker: MS. MAHINDARATNE
utterances.text: Have you seen Sarajevo being shelled from Trebevic? And I'm asking about have you seen, personally.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes, Mr. Piletta-Zanin.

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Mr. President, I think the witness has already answered this type of question on two occasions.

utterances.speaker: MS. MAHINDARATNE
utterances.text: Very well, Mr. President. I will ask any next question.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes, yes, please go ahead.

utterances.speaker: MS. MAHINDARATNE
utterances.text: -- Given that you did not see Sarajevo being shelled from Serb territory, how do you explain your statement, and I'm referring to transcript page 17176 -- you were questioned: "Witness, I'm going to interrupt you. What do you know about the targets that were shelled by the Serbian forces in Sarajevo? My question is as a general rule and what nature of these targets, if you know anything about this." And your answer is, "I think that there was" -- "they were, I think is what you meant to say," they were in response to fire from Sarajevo and targeted the targets from which they were active." You also testified further - and I'm referring to transcript page number 17184 - you say, "But in my prior testimony, I kept repeating that they shot from Trebevic mostly when the Serbs were provoked, and that is when they shelled the town." Now, Witness, if you did not see personally Sarajevo being shelled from the Serb territory, how do you know that the shelling was in fact in response to firing from Sarajevo?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DP2 [Resumed]
utterances.text: I know that because each attack from Sarajevo was made known to us because the sirens were sounded. And whenever the mobile mortars appeared, return fire was always opened as a result. And as I said, it was the Serb forces responding.

utterances.speaker: MS. MAHINDARATNE
utterances.text: Moving on to another area. You testified with regard to damage caused to structures within the city of Sarajevo in this manner - and I am referring to your testimony here, transcript page number 17048 - "in the old part of the town, including the centre, not a single mosque or minaret were destroyed." Then in reference to the old part of town and Bistrik, you said, "Not a single building was destroyed. Only damage was to the roofs and the windows." That was your testimony.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DP2 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. MAHINDARATNE
utterances.text: Witness, where is the central post office building located?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DP2 [Resumed]
utterances.text: It's across the road from the faculty of law, on the same side as the faculty of law in the centre of town.

utterances.speaker: MS. MAHINDARATNE
utterances.text: Wasn't the central post office building completely destroyed?

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Objection, Mr. President.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Objection.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: What's your objection, Mr. Piletta-Zanin?

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: [Interpretation] It's twofold. Time has expired. And secondly, this is outside the time frame of the indictment. And also, I think that the decision of your Trial Chamber specifies this fact.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] If I may answer that question.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: [Previous interpretation continues] ...

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] The main post office --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Let us first decide on the --

utterances.speaker: MS. MAHINDARATNE
utterances.text: Can I respond, Mr. President?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. MAHINDARATNE
utterances.text: This is an issue which goes to the credibility of the witness, because the witness has in general terms testified that the only damage he's witnessed in the city was damage to the roofs and the windows.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. You don't have to further explain. Apart from that, that's my recollection that a lot of questions were put, especially also in respect of the time frame outside and chief, and examination-in-chief and the time frame outside the time frame of the -- of the indictment. You may put this question to the witness. The witness can answer the question. But your time is then over, Ms. Mahindaratne.

utterances.speaker: MS. MAHINDARATNE
utterances.text: May I be permitted just one more question?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: I beg your pardon?

utterances.speaker: MS. MAHINDARATNE
utterances.text: May I be permitted just one more question after the witness answers that question, sir?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: If it's just one question, please then put the question to the witness and we'll then decide if the witness is allowed to answer your next question.

utterances.speaker: MS. MAHINDARATNE
utterances.text: Very well.

utterances.speaker: MS. MAHINDARATNE
utterances.text: Will you please answer my question first. I'm sorry, I didn't ask you. Wasn't the central main post office building which is located in the centre of the town destroyed?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DP2 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Not a single citizen from Sarajevo will tell you that the post office has been damaged in any way. [Indiscernible] that a single wall was missing. It was set on fire, but it doesn't destroyed like the town hall. That simply is not the case.

utterances.speaker: MS. MAHINDARATNE
utterances.text: You yourself admit that this building was set on fire, yet your testimony was that the only damage you saw in the city was the roofs and the windows. I put it to you, witness, that your testimony with regard to damage caused to the structures within the city is incorrect.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: You may answer that question.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I said that the old part of town and the centre -- that it didn't look like damage at the line of demarcation. I say that not a single building was destroyed, apart from the fact that a wall had perhaps been penetrated by a shell. But I stand by my claim that not a single building was destroyed.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. MAHINDARATNE
utterances.text: That concludes the cross-examination.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Thank you, Ms. Mahindaratne. Is there any need to re-examine the witness? Please proceed.

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes, thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: [Interpretation] The map is still on the ELMO apparently. Witness, I would like you to focus on the map. It's just a matter I would like to clarify.

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Could we focus -- could we zoom into the centre of the map, the zone which is between points 7 and 8.

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: Witness --

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: [Interpretation] We still don't have the same versions of the map, Mr. President. I would have liked to show the witness the same map, the map which is identical to the one that I have in front of me. But it's slightly different, as far as the chronology is concerned. May I do so? May I show the witness a slightly different version of the map.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: A different version of the map?

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes. It's just a prior or subsequent version, but -- an earlier or later version, but it's the same type of map.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. Please do so.

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you very much. With the assistance of the usher. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Is there a number for that map, Mr. Piletta-Zanin?

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: [Interpretation] No, Madam Registrar. We are not going to give it a number. I would just like the witness to focus on the map, to find his bearings.

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: Witness, do you recognise the area that you have in front of you, in the centre of the screen? Witness, I'm referring to the exit of the tunnel. Can you see any buildings there? And there are three letters there, "FAK" to the left of the letter "H" which indicates a hospital. Can you see that?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DP2 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: I didn't hear your answer.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DP2 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I can see it.

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: Thank you. What do these three letters mean "FAK"?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DP2 [Resumed]
utterances.text: If you're referring to this location that I am pointing at --

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DP2 [Resumed]
utterances.text: That is the faculty of architecture.

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: Thank you. Are these buildings -- are these the buildings where you said that you saw the tanks?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DP2 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, exactly.

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: Thank you. Please take the map which is below -- beneath this one, with the assistance of the usher. Yes. Gently. Thank you. Witness, could you point to these faculty buildings, please.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DP2 [Resumed]
utterances.text: [Indicates]

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: Thank you. The witness pointed to the buildings slightly to the north of the exit of the tunnel between points 7 and 8 in a somewhat triangular zone. Thank you. Witness, I would now like you to go back to what you mentioned a minute ago. At page 25 -- 25, 25 you mentioned sirens. I would like you to tell us why these sirens were sounded. That's the first question. And then, was it a mechanism that was systematically employed or was it an exception, et cetera, et cetera?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DP2 [Resumed]
utterances.text: The inhabitants of Bistrik were used to this. The sirens would always indicate when an attack was going to be carried, an attack that had already been expected for months. And each time there was an attack, these sirens would be sounded. Whether it was organised or not, well, people in town always spoke about attacks, when there were attacks that were launched. And when they did talk about this, about these attacks, then the sirens would be sounded. And there would always be an attack when the sirens were sounded. And this was really quite frequent.

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: Thank you. Witness, to make sure that everything is as clear as possible, did people fire from the platform, or was it necessary to take the weapon off in order to fire from the ground or from some other level?

utterances.speaker: MS. MAHINDARATNE
utterances.text: Mr. President, I object.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. MAHINDARATNE
utterances.text: The issue of manner of firing from this so-called mobile mortars was not dealt with in cross-examination.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Piletta-Zanin.

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Mr. President, I'll respond to that question gladly, to the question put -- the question that my learned colleague asked had to do with the three sides of the vehicle, not four sides. But I just wanted to know whether fire was opened from -- in a certain way or not, whether the object was -- whether the vehicle was covered or not. And I think that this question does have a certain technical aspect.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: You may ask one or two questions in this respect. But please keep in mind, Mr. Piletta-Zanin, that the cross-examination was about the platform and not on whether one was shooting from the ground or from the vehicle. Please proceed.

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: Witness, as far as you know, the platform that we have spoken about, did this platform make it possible for fire to be opened from it?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DP2 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, the purpose of the platform was such: Fire was opened from the platform.

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: Thank you. Thank you very much. Now, Witness, I'd like us to go back to another thing that you mentioned briefly. You said that local population tried to get rid of those mobile weapons and didn't want them in their streets. Could you please elaborate on this.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DP2 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Your Honours, this was really something. It was more than once that I was present when the population was getting out in the street very vocally telling them to go away. And they would say to these people, "Why are you provoking them? Why are you doing this when they are peaceful?" And on one occasion, one of the people of the -- from the platform responded, "We are doing this to get their response."

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: Could you please elaborate on this last point. You said that you heard somebody who said this. Was this a soldier? Was this somebody from the crew?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DP2 [Resumed]
utterances.text: No. These were the citizens of that part of the town. They would get out of their houses. These were women, people who were retired, old people who went out in the street and wanted the mobile mortar to leave their street, their part of town.

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: Very well. I'm going to repeat my question. The person who said "we wanted a response," this person, was this a citizen or was this a soldier, somebody who was a member of the mortar crew?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DP2 [Resumed]
utterances.text: A soldier on the platform.

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: Thank you very much. Was he in uniform; yes or no?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DP2 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: Thank you very much.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Piletta-Zanin, this issue has been raised in chief, not this cross. So I allowed you to ask a few questions on it and --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Please proceed, Mr. Piletta-Zanin.

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: Now we're going to change the subject. Witness, you spoke to us about the shelling that occurred when delegations from various parliaments or journalists arrived in the town. Do you recall what you told us?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DP2 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: Thank you. Did you have any information at the time about a certain delegation coming or a television crew coming, et cetera? And if you did, how was that?

utterances.speaker: MS. MAHINDARATNE
utterances.text: Mr. President, I object.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Piletta-Zanin, I think that Ms. Mahindaratne is not quite happy at this very moment because she asked for specific incidents where that would happen, and the witness has testified that he could not specify. So therefore, if you can now --

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Mr. President.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I apologise, but my question was not to find out if this witness knew about a specific visit but whether he was able to find out through the media information about the fact that a commission or delegation was going to come. My question is completely different. I apologise. Again, I was misunderstood.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Could you tell us, Mr. DP2, more about the -- what you knew and what your recollection is now on such incidents that firing took place at the moment where delegations put -- or journalists or reporters were expected to arrive?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] How I found out about this information: When there was electricity, it would be through the television. When there was no electricity, then it would be on the radio. And now the question where would I get the electricity: I had a battery of my car, and I would manage to have this -- to use this to get information. And --

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: Could the witness repeat this answer, please.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Could you please repeat the last part of your answer. You said, "And I would manage to have this -- to use this to get information." You were then talking about the battery of your car. Could you please repeat the last part of your --

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] The battery, yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. And you would use that, and what did you then say?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] After that, I said that the information about visits to Sarajevo were acquired through our mutual communications, people communicating with each other, from people talking to each other. Acquaintances, friends, and so on, neighbours.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: But it's still not quite clear to me. Did you learn about those visits of reporters or delegations from the television, or are you telling us that when you had no electricity -- or no car battery, that you would then learn that from what people would tell you on the street?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes, precisely, because there were apartments -- friends of mine, acquaintances, who regularly received information. They were able to listen to the TV and the radio. These were our neighbours who received the electricity from generators.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. And would they tell you prior to the visits that they would take place, or would they tell you -- or did you see it on television once they had taken place?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] It was always that the delegation would be announced either on TV or the radio. Each visit was announced.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Please proceed, Mr. Piletta-Zanin.

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you, Mr. President.

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: Witness, in relation to what you have told us, could you please answer the following question: What was the frequency of acts of provocation that you spoke of earlier in relation to the arrivals of those delegations, either parliamentary delegations, reporters, or any other delegations?

utterances.speaker: MS. MAHINDARATNE
utterances.text: Mr. President, I object.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes, Ms. Mahindaratne.

utterances.speaker: MS. MAHINDARATNE
utterances.text: Mr. President, this aspect was not dealt in cross-examination, the frequency --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Well, it's so close to what you asked the witness that I would deny the objection. You may answer the question, Mr. DP2.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes. It's a difficult question, what was the frequency. But if I am allowed to say, I would have to say that there was something happening all the time. Basically every fortnight, every month. That would be my estimate.

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: Witness, my question was in relation to the frequency of incidents related to the arrivals of those delegations. That is, was there something that was systematic, something absolute, that every visit could entail incidents, or was this something rare and so on what can you tell us about that?

utterances.speaker: MS. MAHINDARATNE
utterances.text: Mr. President, I object. Inviting the witness to speculate. Systematic --

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Mr. President.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Please.

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I allowed myself to say this in order to make the witness understand the question. I took two extremes, the rare occurrence and the frequent occurrence in the other case.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Your question was whether it was something rare and what can you tell us about that. I mean, the -- that's at least what I read in my transcript.

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: [Interpretation] No, Mr. President. That was not my question. My question was about the frequency of incidents in relation to these visits by delegations. Was this something systematic or contrary to that, something that was rare? So I gave two hypotheses.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. Let's first try to understand what you mean by "this," whether this was something systematic. Did you want to know from the witness whether such a provocative action would be a systematic response to the -- you say "this." So what Mr. Piletta-Zanin asks you, Mr. DP2 - please tell us - whether in your experience such provocative fire would regularly occur when such visits would take place or whether this would only incidentally happen at these occasions.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Well, in the town the way we felt shelling, one couldn't call it an incident. (redacted)

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: (redacted) But if we are speaking about other locations around the town,then that would be an occurrence, because there was a very frequent shooting but it was in different locations.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. But I don't know whether you understood the question well. The question was whether -- let me put it in a simple way, whether you would expect provocative fire to take place whenever journalists or delegations of parliamentarians would visit Sarajevo or that only in a few -- at a few of such occasions - that means of such visits - you would experience such provocative fire.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Not that we expected whether it would happen, but it really always happened whenever there were parliamentarians or any other delegations, journalists, reporters, writers. There would always be this provocation. Really.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: That's the answer. Please proceed.

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you, Mr. President.

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: I'm going to change the subject, and I'd like to have a map back on the ELMO, please.

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I'm told that we're supposed to have a break soon, Mr. President. I don't know.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: We'll have a break soon. But how much time would you still need, Mr. Piletta-Zanin?

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Five or six minutes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Let's try to finish in five or six minutes.

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Very well.

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: Witness, you spoke to us earlier in relation to one of the locations where the army was located. You spoke to us about a school near the brewery. And it appears in the English transcript as being the catering school.

utterances.speaker: MS. MAHINDARATNE
utterances.text: Mr. President.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. MAHINDARATNE
utterances.text: The witness did not speak about a school near the brewery.

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I am not sure, Mr. President.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Neither am I. So if there's any doubt, would you please -- but I'll try to find it.

utterances.speaker: MS. MAHINDARATNE
utterances.text: I don't think it's proper for Defence counsel to converse in loud tones in the presence of the witness.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes, ma'am.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Did you intend to say, Mr. Piletta-Zanin -- because it has been translated in a way -- was that the meaning of your words? Would you please look at the transcript.

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Which page, Mr. President?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: "A vos ordres", it has been translated as "yes, ma'am." Is that what you intended to express?

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Almost, Mr. President.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Then please show proper respect for a --

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Absolutely.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: [Previous interpretation continues] ... Made by Ms. Mahindaratne and not address her in these kind of words. Please proceed, and indicate to us where the school is to be found.

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes, Mr. President. It seems -- I don't know whether the witness can perhaps take his --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: No. The only issue at stake is --

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: [Interpretation] -- Headphones off --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Whether the words that have been used --

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Precisely, in order to find out about this.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. I would rather find it in the transcript, Mr. Piletta-Zanin.

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Mr. President, I can see on page 33, line 15 and 16 something that corresponds to what I believe that I said before I was interrupted -- before I was interrupted. Can you see that?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: I haven't found it yet. One moment.

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Excuse me?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: I have not found it yet.

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Do you want me to read it? I can read the following, with your leave. [In English] "A catering school near the brewery, and there were other schools which were also used." [Interpretation] My line -- but I don't know what the transcript is -- my line is line 15 and line 16 of page 33, Mr. President.

utterances.speaker: MS. MAHINDARATNE
utterances.text: Yes. I see that, Mr. President. It says "catering school near the brewery." I stand corrected.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. And you should have refrained from objecting. Please proceed.

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Mr. President, I'd like that in the future if there is an objection, that we can all be certain of that. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: Now, I'd like you, Witness, to point on the map, to use the pointer. And if you can show us exactly on the map where this famous catering school was, as it was stated in the transcript, a catering school near the brewery. Could you please point to it with the pointer, Witness, please.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DP2 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Excuse me. Why this school? Why this catering school? I meant the other school. You mean the school in Bistrik or ...?

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: Yes, Witness. The school that you mentioned in which there were soldiers that were stationed, the school near the old brewery, sometimes known as the old brewery. If you can indicate this, let us know, please.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Could the map please be moved such that we can see where the witness points at.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Indicates]

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: Very well. Thank you. Is that the location that you're indicating? Could you please take a black pen and put a black cross. And if you can place a cross and a number -- just a moment. Just a moment. The number that is supposed to follow the black numbers that you have used on the map.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: We've used only numbers, whether black or blue. So I would say that the last number has been "9" as far as I -- my recollection goes. That would be --

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Very well. Very well.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DP2 [Resumed]
utterances.text: [Marks]

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: Thank you. Witness, to continue on the subject of schools, I'd like to clarify something that seems to be an error that comes or stems from the difficulties in relation to the language. You were asked a question to find out if you were digging the trenches next to a certain school, and there was a confusion that resulted from this. What happened? Why did you mention this school, in relation to the trenches? Simply, in a nutshell.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DP2 [Resumed]
utterances.text: I think it was taken out of the context of my testimony, but I really never dug any trenches behind the school.

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: Very well. But what happened there? Was there, I don't know, any need to quote this school in relation to the trenches?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DP2 [Resumed]
utterances.text: In this school was located the troops of the 10th Mountain Brigade, and mentioned along with the school there was -- in the yard of that school there was a mortar there.

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: The question, one before last, in relation to the -- no, not -- no need to do that, Mr. President. It's already been established. Another question: Witness, you have told us that in your mind, as far as you recall, Serb shelling came from Trebevic as frequently as Muslim forces wished this to happen. That was your testimony on page 55, line 3. My question is the following: In relation to the old town and the parts of the town that you knew there, the shellings in these parts, did they seem to you to be very intense, intense? What can you tell us about the intensity of these shellings in these areas? And I'm talking about Serb shellings of these areas. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MS. MAHINDARATNE
utterances.text: Mr. President, I object. That's an area that has not been touched upon in cross-examination at all, the frequency of shelling in the old part of the town and Bistrik.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Piletta-Zanin.

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes, Mr. President. I believe that the situation is the same as that from before. This is very close to the subject dealt with in cross-examination by the Prosecution. Therefore, it will be useful to know this.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. The -- you may answer the question, Witness.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I have a short -- a brief answer to give. After each announced attack, there would be a shelling of the town with the announcement of the attack and the shelling. All this would last some 10, 20 minutes. And after that, you could take a walk in the town.

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: [Interpretation] And vice versa.

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: Witness, do you remember attacks from Trebevic which were not followed by sirens -- which the sirens did not follow?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DP2 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. There were such attacks -- well, not attacks, but there were some shells that landed on the town, and that happened on occasions when it would be announced that some building -- there was fabrication, manufacturing of weapons. There were troops located in some building. But most of the time it was the weapons manufacturing. I know that in Bistrik that's how three shells landed there. And following those shells, I heard the following story in the streets, that all the Serbs should --

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: I'm going to interrupt you, Witness.

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Mr. President, for the transcript, my question in French was the opposite what was -- what is in the English transcript. If the witness recalled attacks that were not announced by the sirens, that is, that did not follow the sirens. Not the other way around. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: It will be corrected. But if I just -- the question is whether there were any attacks or at least shelling not preceded by sirens.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] There were individual shells that would land on certain targets. These targets were most frequently caused by an information that there were weapons manufactured in a building. And

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. And then -- five to six minutes --

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: [Interpretation] No more questions. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: We'll adjourn until quarter past 6.00.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Could the witness be escorted into the courtroom. Mr. DP2, Judge Nieto-Navia has one or more questions for you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE NIETO-NAVIA
utterances.text: Thank you, Mr. President. Could the map 1817 be shown to the witness. Mr. Witness, you said that number 8 at the Ciglane tunnel was wrongly put there. Could you take a red pen and mark the right spot.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DP2 [Resumed]
utterances.text: [Marks]

utterances.speaker: JUDGE NIETO-NAVIA
utterances.text: Could you make a circle and put the number "8" inside.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DP2 [Resumed]
utterances.text: [Marks]

utterances.speaker: JUDGE NIETO-NAVIA
utterances.text: Thank you. And it was almost the same with the faculty. Do you remember that? Would you do the same exercise?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DP2 [Resumed]
utterances.text: [Marks]

utterances.speaker: JUDGE NIETO-NAVIA
utterances.text: Thank you. And finally, you mentioned the school where the Caco's troops were billeted. Do you remember that? Would you put a red circle and an "S" inside, please.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DP2 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Number 9?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE NIETO-NAVIA
utterances.text: Oh, it's number 9. I'm sorry. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DP2 [Resumed]
utterances.text: [Marks]

utterances.speaker: JUDGE NIETO-NAVIA
utterances.text: Okay. No further questions, Mr. President.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. Judge El Mahdi has one or more questions for you as well.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE EL MAHDI
utterances.text: Thank you, Mr. President. [Interpretation] Yes. Witness, you said that in your opinion the shots from the city, their purpose was to provoke a reaction on the part of the enemy side. And you came to this conclusion -- this was your opinion because of what the inhabitants said. They were afraid that shots being fired from the vicinity of the homes would have a certain result, and they said, "Don't shoot, because this will provoke enemy fire." If I have understood you correctly, you yourself analysed the purpose that the other side was pursuing, the objective the other side was pursuing. And if I have understood you correctly, you came to the conclusion that the Serbian side was aiming at military objectives. How did you arrive at this conclusion?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DP2 [Resumed]
utterances.text: My position wasn't based on what people said but on the basis of my own experience in Sarajevo. I haven't had the opportunity of showing you another 20 locations in Sarajevo where the BH army was billeted, in all schools, nurseries, universities, and in office buildings, company buildings. And I am really claiming this on the basis of my personal experience up until May of 1994. I don't know whether fire was ever opened without this having been provoked or without there being sirens which were sounded when Muslim forces were attacking or carrying out attack against the Serbian positions, and this is the truth.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE EL MAHDI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] To tell you the truth, with regard to the mobile mortars, there is something that is bothering me, because the fact that they are mobile, I find it difficult to understand. I find it difficult to understand your conclusions. Was the Serb side targeting these mortars or other objectives?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DP2 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, this doesn't only have to do with mobile mortars. I've indicated those six mortars at the ring road to the right. We could refer to the image again, to the map. And I indicated the mobile mortars which would move from one street to another. And it's -- and most frequently the pass -- the objective was the place from which fire had been opened, and that is the place that the Serbs would direct fire to when responding.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE EL MAHDI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes. But the response was directed at the place from which the mortar had been fired? I'll repeat that perhaps. You're not hearing the translation?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DP2 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. It's fine now.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE EL MAHDI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] So the response was directed at the location of the mobile mortars. Because if I have understood you correctly, you said that the inhabitants of a neighbourhood where these mobile mortars were located, they were afraid of reprisals being taken and directed at their houses. So if I've understood you correctly, the Serbian side did target the places from which these mortars had been fired.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DP2 [Resumed]
utterances.text: [No audible response]

utterances.speaker: JUDGE EL MAHDI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] And this is not necessarily a military objective. Rather, the location is not a military objective. I'm not talking about the mortars as such.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DP2 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE EL MAHDI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] So the response was directed at a location but not necessarily at the target itself; that is to say, at the mortar itself, which is by nature mobile and can thus easily be moved.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DP2 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, you're quite right. The place from which the mortars were fired was the place that was targeted when fire was returned. You are quite right.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE EL MAHDI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes. Well, thank you. And if I've understood you correctly, you said that the response would usually last for 20 minutes. Is that your testimony, or have I misunderstood you?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DP2 [Resumed]
utterances.text: You've understood me correctly. Twenty minutes from the time the sirens were sounded or the mortars were fired from. Then fire would be returned. They would use a few -- they would fire a few shells. I think that that lasted for between 15 and 20 minutes at the most.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE EL MAHDI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] But my question is: How long did it last, the response, the retaliation itself? I am not talking about when the response commenced. If I have understood you correctly, you said that the response lasted 20 minutes.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DP2 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. It's difficult to say how long the Serbian side took to respond. You have to know that there were inter-Muslim conflicts in the city itself. So these incidents with mortars and -- which included the return of fire from the Serbian side, these incidents were used when Muslims were dealing with each other, when there were conflicts between Muslims. I was present when Caco fired at the other part of town, at Dragan Vikic, in the police centre. He was a well known police commander. So it's difficult for me to say how long this lasted on the Serbian side, because I was in the basement --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE EL MAHDI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] But allow me. Could you just answer my question. How long did the response on the part of the Serbian side last?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DP2 [Resumed]
utterances.text: As I said, between 15 and 20 minutes. But this included inter-Muslim conflicts in the city, conflicts between the Muslims themselves in the city. That's my final answer.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE EL MAHDI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you. You said that you witnessed shots being fired from mobile mortars. You said you witnessed shells being fired from mobile mortars.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DP2 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE EL MAHDI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] And you said that the person who fired these shells was in uniform, was a member of the military in uniform. And the vehicle, was it possible to recognise the vehicle as a military vehicle on the basis of its colours?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DP2 [Resumed]
utterances.text: I wouldn't say it was a military vehicle. We called a vehicle a TAM, a T-A-M. It's a small lorry, a one and a half tonne lorry, and this anti-aircraft machine-gun or mortar is mounted on that lorry and then fire is opened from this vehicle. It stops in a street. It fires some shots, and then it goes to another street.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE EL MAHDI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] But was it possible to recognise the vehicle easily as a vehicle which belonged to the army?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DP2 [Resumed]
utterances.text: No. It was an ordinary TAM lorry. And as far as I know, the army didn't use such lorries. It was a city vehicle which had been modified for these purposes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE EL MAHDI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] And, for example, you didn't notice -- observe Volkswagen cars, vehicles. There were only vehicles of other makes that you saw, that you could see? I think that you said that you saw fire being opened from these vehicles on five or six occasions -- four or five occasions. So these weren't really Volkswagen vehicles.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DP2 [Resumed]
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE EL MAHDI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you very much.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. DP2, I've got a few questions for you as well. And I would like to draw your attention to your testimony in respect of a shell falling in people queuing for bread. You said you were involved in it. Could you, first of all, tell us exactly where that is, whether it's on this map. And could you please point at it. You said it was in Vasa Miskin Street, as far as I remember.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DP2 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. This street is now called Ferhadija Street, but it was Vasa Miskin.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Could you please with a red pen point to make a circle and a cross and add -- I think it would be number -- would it be 11?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DP2 [Resumed]
utterances.text: [Marks]

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. Could you tell me, how long was that queue? How many people were queuing for bread?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DP2 [Resumed]
utterances.text: The queue was 50 metres long, and there were up to three or four people lined up in the -- in the queue. I was at the end of the queue -- three or four people abreast in the queue.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. Do you know how many people were injured or killed?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DP2 [Resumed]
utterances.text: I think about 20, 25 people -- no, that's the amount of people who were killed. That's the number of people who were killed. But far more people were wounded.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. You were in that queue as well?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DP2 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Were you injured?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DP2 [Resumed]
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Could you tell me how wide is that street is. Is it, first of all -- yes, first of all, how wide is it?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DP2 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, 5 or 6 metres. It's a narrow street.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: It's a narrow street.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DP2 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Between 5 and 7 metres, not more.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. And you told us that it was exceptional that people had to queue outside for bread; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DP2 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. A little further below, that's where you received that bread, from the Romanija cinema. There was a passageway there, and that's where we would wait. That's where we were. When the lorry would come, they would give us the bread and we would give them coupons as money. And the first time a shell fell, we were taken out to this position. It's the only direction that is open to -- in the direction of the Serbs in Borije. That's where a shell can come from. And we were wondering why they took us out there, since all the shops in Titova Street were empty and the bread could have been distributed there. So why at this location where what happened to us happened?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: It's not quite clear to me. You said, "And the first time a shell fell." Were you then already queuing outside when the first shell fell?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DP2 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Only one shell fell.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Only one shell fell.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DP2 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: And is that street where you had to queue, is that going east-west or north-south? How should I on this map interpret your marking? Is the street from the left to the right or from bottom to the top on this map?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DP2 [Resumed]
utterances.text: If we go in the direction of this sign, it's along the Miljacka River. If we go in the direction of the markings, it's the south-eastern part.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. That would mean more, rather, west-east rather than north-south. Is that a correct understanding of your answer?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DP2 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. Yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: You say that you were taken out to a place facing from where Serb shells could have come from. If I look at this map, am I right in understanding that both to the north and to the south at a distance of approximately 2 to 3 kilometres there would be Serbian positions?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DP2 [Resumed]
utterances.text: That street is so narrow, and the buildings are fairly high. So it's not possible for a shell to fall from the left and the right-hand side, from the Serbian positions. To the extent that I understand ballistics, it couldn't have been fired from this street in order to fall here. It could only have fallen -- come from the Serbian positions that I'm indicating here, which is where I dug trenches in Borije.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Could we please zoom out so that -- Would you please point again to the Serbian positions in your view would be the only ones from where such a -- The witness --

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DP2 [Resumed]
utterances.text: It's not on the map. It would be approximately here. From Miskin Street, you can see Serb positions. From that location, you can see them.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: The witness -- the witness points at the edge of the map where the word "Sarajevo" has been cut into "Sarajev" just below where he marked that he had had to dig trenches. So the shells -- at least that was suggested that the shells might have come from the north-eastern direction; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DP2 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Now, where would the shells have come from in your view? Because your answer suggests that it was not a shell that came from a Serbian position but, rather, from a BiH position. Could you indicate what position you thought as a possible origin of fire.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DP2 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, when we lived in Sarajevo, according to the imprint of a shell on the asphalt, we would always be able to recognise as good experts where the shell could have come from.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. Where did it come from, in your view?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DP2 [Resumed]
utterances.text: In this case, according to the imprint, the -- where the directions where the shrapnel had gone, they went to all directions with the same frequency. If it had gone in one -- from one direction, then it would have gone in the opposite way. We would always know that if the traces were on one side, that the shell would have come from the other side. But even today you can see that the traces, the imprints, are going star-like, all around the trace, which confirms that this came almost vertically. And I believe that my statement is true, that it is most probably that this shell was fired by their own forces on their own people. That is my explanation. This is what I believe on the basis of why I think we found ourselves precisely there -- found us there in this -- and I was told this by this man from the 10th Mountain Brigade who told me that this was done by their own side. I cannot claim this is true, but I believe this is my position, that this could have been their own shell fired on their own people.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. From where would it have been fired, then, in order to fall almost vertically on that place?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DP2 [Resumed]
utterances.text: If it is true, the information I received, then it was fired from Planika, from the same building before the war. It used to be a shoe store. It was called Planika. And it was fired --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Could you indicate on the map where that is. Could you perhaps first point at it and --

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DP2 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Here, next to this circle on the left-hand side, on the left side - not on the right side- what looks like a building here.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Could you please -- could we perhaps first zoom in on that place. And then could you please indicate precisely where your situate Planika.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DP2 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, I -- this is where it is. This is where the location of the firing would be. This is where I just indicated, here.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Do I understand that that's a very short distance of -- I mean, that's a matter of, perhaps, 50, 60, 70 metres from the place where the shell landed?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DP2 [Resumed]
utterances.text: No. It was dropped from the top of the building. That is, 3 metres to the right.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: It was dropped from the building. That's what you were told, or is that your --

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DP2 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. Yes. That's the information that I told you about, a protected piece of information.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Protected in what way? You mean the man who told you. You mentioned his name, I think, and -- yes. So that shell was --

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DP2 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, that's right. Yes, I told you this. Yes. And from the high-rise building of JAT, Yugoslav airlines, there was a sniper who was active from the eighth or ninth floor, and I heard this sniper. And after that there was an information that this sniper had been strangled in the toilet while the other two that fired this shell, they were killed. That's the information that I have.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: So the shell was fired or thrown?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DP2 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Thrown.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. Have you seen any of this by yourself, or is this just the explanation given to you later on by the person you mentioned?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DP2 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Personally, I can only say that when I was there, I heard sniping from a high-rise building and that this sniper, he did snipe, it's true. About a year after that there was a friend of mine who spoke on TV and who said that he lived in the Planika building where he lived. And when it happened, he went downstairs to help those that were wounded and killed. And from the JAT skyscraper, there was a sniper that was firing and was just creating even more chaos, and then it turned out that there was this -- there was a Serb man that was in the toilet. So my question was: If it was a Serb man who was strangled in the toilet, then my question was why was he strangled? Why wasn't he taken out to be tried, and why weren't we told that this happened? So that's why I believe that this shell was thrown.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DP2 [Resumed]
utterances.text: I believe that's how it happened.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Did the shell fall in the middle of the queue or at the far end or at the beginning of the queue?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DP2 [Resumed]
utterances.text: It fell next to the queue, about 10 metres from the beginning of the queue. It was closer to the beginning of the queue, the front end of the queue than to the end of the queue. It didn't actually fall on the citizens there.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: And the people in the queue were, therefore, never further away than some 40, 45 metres from where the shell landed. Is that -- or not more than 50 metres; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DP2 [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, sir. There were two or three metres from where the shell landed. The shell landed next to the queue.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. You said that some -- I don't know the exact number, but a high number of people were killed and far more were injured. How did you escape from any injury in this incident being in the queue?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DP2 [Resumed]
utterances.text: I was at the end of the queue. At the end of the queue there was a Bosna folklore shop, and I was at the very end of the queue, and the shell didn't touch me. And I'm not the only one who was not wounded. Many of us were not injured.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Thank you for your answers. My next question would be about what you said, that sometimes shells would fall without previous siren warnings, and that would be if the -- if information would have been received about manufacturing plants of weaponry. Do you remember saying that?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DP2 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. When you said that this was in response to information received on manufacturing plants, what did you know about the information received by those who fired the shells prior to firing them?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DP2 [Resumed]
utterances.text: My information was very limited. I couldn't know anything in particular. What I did know is that the street where I live in, three such shells landed on a building about which neighbours and citizens who were passing by told me, "You see, this is the fifth column working." These were the fifth column, meaning the people who were telling the other side what was happening. "How would the Serbs otherwise know that there were weapons being manufactured here. They should all be killed." So that's what I'm telling you. Sometimes shells land when there were no provocations from the town.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: That was your conclusion, that the Serbs must have been informed about the presence of a manufacturing plant there.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DP2 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. Yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Did you ever yourself pass any information to the other side of the confrontation line?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DP2 [Resumed]
utterances.text: No. But when I left the town, I testified about what was happening in the town.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. Thank you. I have no further questions for you. Is there any need to re-examine the witness on -- yes, please, Mr. Piletta-Zanin.

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Witness, there were three or four subjects that need to be looked at again, the first being in relation to a question asked by Judge El Mahdi. You were asked a question about the length of the shelling. Do you remember that question?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DP2 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: Thank you. I'm going to quote now the President, who was quoting you. Page 26, line 21. And this is what the President told you, in English: [In English] "And after ten minutes, there would be a response and the shells would start falling." [Interpretation] End of quote. I'm interested in these ten minutes. You were told about a period of 20 minutes. When you answered affirmatively, when you said yes, did you include in this general period of time these ten minutes of reaction that preceded the action itself?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DP2 [Resumed]
utterances.text: That's what I said. From the --

utterances.speaker: MS. MAHINDARATNE
utterances.text: I object. I object.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. MAHINDARATNE
utterances.text: I object. I think this issue was very well explained by the witness and the Defence counsel is now leading the witness.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. I have no objection against questions, Mr. Piletta-Zanin, but would you please refrain from leading. Please proceed.

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Very well. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: On page 69, line 12 you also mentioned, in relation to shellings, the following, what I'm going to quote: [In English] "-- Conflicts between Muslims themselves in the city." [Interpretation] What do you mean by these conflicts between Muslims themselves in the city? Could you give us an example, please?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DP2 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, that is just a separate topic of this Sarajevo war. It is not unknown that Muslim commanders had divided up the town, not only on areas of war but also areas of looting and robbing their own people. Among themselves, they fought more than fighting the Serb side. They fought about the territory for control, and I would say that each of this Serb response, they tried to attach that to the Serb side. Not just once but more than once I would see from Bistrik that Caco would be firing shells on the police of the other side. So everybody was against the police, and they all fought against each other, and yet they were still all against the police. It was real chaos in the city, and one just had to struggle to survive.

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: Thank you. Witness, third question: In relation to the incident that you witnessed on the street that you mentioned earlier, the Vasa Miskin Street. And on this subject you answered to a question asked by the President saying that in theory the direction of the source of fire would have been more or less that one of north-east. It would have been fire from north-east. Do you recall that?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DP2 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: Thank you. My question is the following: Do you know if - and here I am referring to the direction - if this line of the theoretical source of fire, would it include in its trajectory several positions; yes or no? What I mean by "several positions," I mean several positions of the opposite side.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DP2 [Resumed]
utterances.text: I am unable to know this.

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: Thank you very much.

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: [Interpretation] No further questions.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Thank you, Mr. Piletta-Zanin. Mr. DP2, this concludes your evidence in this court. I think I already once thanked you for coming. I now can thank you for coming twice. And since you look still to be in good shape, I hope that you have just as safe a return home as you had last time. I would ask you to -- just to stay seated until the public gallery has been closed so that the protective measures are in effect. I -- since the parties have not paid specific attention to the pictures you put at their disposal, I would like them to be returned to you by the registrar. And I hope you don't mind that you have done some work which --

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] May I say something?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Well, it depends on what you would like to say. If you would refrain from comments and tell us what you -- I will stop you if there's -- if it's something that I would rather not hear. But please go ahead.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honours, it is with great happiness and with great pleasure that I accepted to come here and testify as a witness. (redacted)

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: What I would like to say - and I don't want to take your time - is that -- well, I better not. I just want to thank you. If I have contributed to enlightening you on the circumstances in wartime Sarajevo, that will be a great pleasure to me, and I wish you good work and a lot of justice in your further work, and I'd like to transmit to General Galic the greetings from the Serb Sarajevo. Thank you very much. And please don't mind if I have abused the opportunity to speak.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. Well, I do understand that you feel that it was good to appear and to tell in this court. We are happy to hear that. Then, Mr. Usher, could you please escort the witness out of the courtroom.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Piletta-Zanin.

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I am going to wait for the witness to leave, Mr. President.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Meanwhile, I can inform you that the decision you are looking forward to has been filed today. So you'll certainly find it.

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you very much.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes. I was just waiting for the witness to leave out of courtesy. I believe, Mr. President, that we are going to have to strike what the witness said about his family background, which is obviously too close to him.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. If that would perhaps be redacted. That would be a wiser thing to do. None of the parties has put questions to him, but ... I just want to express that it's exclusively for these grounds that we strike this from the public record. Madam Registrar, would you please prepare a redaction. We'll then adjourn until tomorrow morning, quarter past 2.00. Madam Registrar, is this in this same courtroom? In this same courtroom. Well, we don't have to wait for the redaction. I'll sign it when we leave the courtroom. We'll adjourn.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: at 7.04 p.m., to be reconvened on Tuesday, the 4th day of February, 2003, at 2.15 p.m.
